title: Continuous orthonormal trivialization conjecture for continuous projector families
statement:
Let $G$ be the underlying group and let $cmathbb{K}^d$ have canonical basis $cxi_1,\dots,\xi_d$. Let $\mathrm{P}:G\to \mathbb{B}_X$ be a continuous projector. For every $g\in G$, choose an orthonormal basis $\{\eta_1^g,\dots,\eta_n^g\}$ of $\operatorname{im}\mathrm{P}(g)$ and an orthonormal basis $\{\eta_{n+1}^g,\dots,\eta_d^g\}$ of $\ker\mathrm{P}(g)$.

**Continuous orthonormal trivialization conjecture.** The bases can be chosen so that the map $T:G\to GL_d(\mathbb{K})$ defined by

$$
T(g)\xi_i=\eta_i^g
$$

is continuous.

This conjecture asks whether every continuous family of projectors admits a continuous choice of orthonormal bases for its image and kernel, equivalently a continuous trivialization adapted to the projector. The supplied text gives no evidence resolving the question.
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2306.17655](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.17655).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.16887

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).
source_name: Néstor Jara and Emir Molina, “Generalized nonautonomous dynamics through groupoid morphisms”, arXiv:2406.16887 (2024).
